page.layout: One printed page of verse and prose, with a running head at the top and page number at the top right; a signature-like mark "L 3" and a catchword "5. There" at the foot. No marginal notes in the text block; show-through from the reverse page is ignored.

l.i: There is my Last and All,

main_text.l: Let me drive in halfa dozen plaine honest
Country Hobnailes, such as the Martyrs
were wont to weare; to make my work
hold the surer; and I have done.
I Fany of these come one

l.i: 1. There lives cannot be good, There, Faith
cannot be sure, Where Truth cannot be quiet,
2. No King can King it right,
Land, As Lands should ruled been,

page.notes: The large initial "T" of stanza 1 is set as a woodcut initial and is joined to "There". The faint mirrored text (show-through from the reverse page) is not transcribed. The word "I" beside the dropped capital and the word "Fany of these come one" are faint and partly illegible in the scan; the line "Fany of these come one" is doubtful.
